La première épidémie en 1973 était circonscrite dans la région du Mayumbe au Bas-Congo.'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. National (Zaire) 1972: no source reports cholera in Zaire before 1973; the national programme dates the first cases to 1973 (Mayumbe, Bas-Congo; Kinshasa 1974) and Taty et al. 2024 (metadata 8) likewise to 1973. INFERRED, not documented: Zaire made no WHO cholera declaration at all before June 1978 (Carme et al. 1983 Tableau III, metadata 40), including during the 1973-1974 western outbreaks, so WHO non-notification is not evidence. Split out of former Index 6 (1970-1972) by Agent 3 (Z1) because the regional situation changed in 1972: REGIONAL CONTEXT (Z6) - neighbour IN EPIDEMIC: Angola declared its first cases in January 1972 (Luanda) and 266 cases in 1972, then spread 'à toute la côte atlantique' (Carme 1983) - Angola is the documented source of the 1973 Mayumbe introduction; Uganda sporadic. Absence beside a neighbouring epidemic rests only on the national programme's retrospective dating, hence confidence 0.5. processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2008-01-01..2017-06-30. Source states: 'In 2017, in addition to the downstream spread along the Congo, suspected cholera cases were reported in inland non-hot spot provinces where no cases had previously been reported during the study timeframe (Figures 2, 3). Source: Ingelbeen et al. 2019, Emerg Infect Dis 25(5):856-864 (metadata 87; re-fetched Europe PMC PMC6478228 full text 2 Oct 2026) - analysis of the national IDSR weekly health-zone surveillance data, January 2008 to week 46 2017 (270,852 suspected cases). Conclusion of the same paper: '...an unexpected increase in cholera cases in inland regions of DRC where no cases had been reported for 15 years'; Table 1 lists the new inland outbreak 'Kwilu, Kwango, Kasai, Lomami, Sankuru | Jul-Nov 2017 | 2,497'. Window 2008-01-01..2017-06-30 = study start to the day before the earliest possible first 2017 case (July 2017). The source applies the 2015 26-province geography to the whole study period. LABEL: Documented_Absence from the national surveillance database (peer-reviewed statement that no cases were reported), but surveillance PARTIAL: the authors caution 'Zero case reporting is not required in the IDSRS, possibly leading to an underestimation of suspected cholera in our analysis, particularly for non-cholera endemic areas where health services might not as readily clinically diagnose and report cholera' - hence confidence 0.6, not 0.9.
